name: Easy in, hard out
definition: Make arriving effortless, and let the structure customers build up be hard to take anywhere else.

mechanism.summary: Adoption costs almost nothing, so customers accumulate structure inside the product: saved credentials, nested pages, linked records. Exports carry the raw data but not the structure, so leaving means rebuilding the thing that made the product useful.

preconditions: Value accumulates in structure specific to the product
No common format holds that structure anywhere else
Customers build it up over months rather than days
failureModes: A rival ships a faithful importer and the advantage disappears
Buyers who check exit costs before signing walk away, which hits enterprise deals hardest

antiPattern.name: Hold the data hostage
antiPattern.description: Refusing export, or letting it quietly fail, turns a structural advantage into a grievance. Grievances are what competitors market against.

relationships.rationale: A product that publishes everything openly on the way in has a harder time justifying structure that is hard to take out.
